proposals.evidence: DEDR4753 gives Tamil maḻai, Malayalam maḻa, Kannada maḻe, Kodagu/Tulu maḷe, Kota may and Toda maw rain. These selected southern survey forms preserve lect-specific lateral, glide, velar or sibilant reflexes and contractions of the rain stem. Minority-lect assignments are comparative extensions; ambiguous source fragments and Indo-Aryan-looking varṣa forms are excluded. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.evidence: DEDR1391 explicitly gives Tamil kaṟi raw or boiled meat/vegetables and Malayalam kaṟi meats/vegetables/hot condiments. These southern survey kari meat responses select the meat sense of that culinary family, retaining the source non-retroflex rhotic spelling. Precise inter-lect transmission is not established by the widespread culinary term alone. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

The selected southern survey vaḷi/vaśi/vagi/vayi/veyi/bayi responses preserve lect reflexes or loss of medial ḻ and initial v/b variation. These are comparative minority-lect extensions; longer phrases and English road responses are excluded. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.evidence: DEDR1254 gives Tamil kayiṟu, Malayalam kayaṟu rope/cord and Kodagu kērï. Selected survey kayir-/kavar-/kagar-/kahar- forms are proposed comparative lect reflexes of the same rope stem, preserving intervocalic glide, labial, velar or fricative notation. More divergent Muthuvan kadɨrɨ/kadarɨ responses are excluded pending stronger sound evidence. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

proposals.evidence: DEDR449 gives Tamil iṭai/iṭam left, Malayalam iṭam/eṭam, Kannada eḍa and Kodagu ëḍate left. These selected simple southern iḍat-/eḍat-/iḍa/eḍa responses preserve the left-side family and ordinary adjectival endings. Longer side/hand compounds and Indo-Aryan ḍāva/ḍebri-type terms remain separate. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.
